title: `ResourceLoader::load` behaves inconsistent for builtin resources
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.dev.custom_build [c4a893e98]
v4.6.1.stable.flathub [14d19694e]

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev (c4a893e98) - Fedora Linux 43 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor

### Issue description

Packed scenes can have builtin resources. Those have a well defined path e.g. `res://scene.tscn::CanvasItemMaterial_drvgu`.

`ResourceLoader::load` loads resources by a given path however when given such paths the method behaves inconsistent, depending on the current state of the cache.

`ResourceLoader::load("res://scene.tscn::CanvasItemMaterial_drvgu")` works and returns the correct resource if the outer scene is currently loaded somewhere (so it is present in the cache).

When calling `ResourceLoader::load("res://scene.tscn::CanvasItemMaterial_drvgu")` without prior loading of `scene.tscn` it will fail.

This is bad, because users are not supposed to care about the resource cache when writing normal code. The presence of something in the cache can make users believe that their code is working correctly, but under certain edge cases it might fail due to something getting unreferenced.

I'd expect to either get a consistent descriptive error. Or preferably to be able to "cold load" builtin resources.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open the MRP
- Run the editor script
- modify whether to first load the scene
- see how it influences the result of the method

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[load_builtin.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25460002/load_builtin.zip)
